changes.before: Mark the collection date with a matching machine-readable value.
changes.after: Give a date a form that people and computers can read.

before: time marks a date, time or duration. For this lesson use a calendar date. Its datetime attribute supplies a machine-readable value, while the text inside supplies the words readers see.

A calendar date here uses four-digit year, two-digit month and two-digit day, separated by hyphens: YYYY-MM-DD. This is not a promise that any arbitrary date-like string is valid. The actual month and day must also form a valid date.

Place this fragment in body. ```html

Next meeting: 8 November.

``` A reader sees 8 November. The attribute also provides the year, 2026. Changing only the visible text leaves datetime unchanged, which can create conflicting information.

Write a collection date of 3 December 2026. Use exactly Thursday, 3 December as the visible wording and the matching normalized attribute. These checks compare the two supplied representations; the lesson does not parse locale-dependent dates or create calendar appointments.
after: Use `<time>` to mark a date. The words inside it are what readers see. Its `datetime` attribute gives the same date in a form that software can read.
For a calendar date, write `datetime` as year-month-day. Use four digits for the year and two each for the month and day. Keep the hyphens between them.

This date has two forms that mean the same thing. ```html

Next meeting: 8 November.

``` `` marks the date. `datetime="2026-11-08"` means 8 November 2026. `8 November` is the text shown on the page. If you change the date, update both forms.
Wrap `Thursday, 3 December` in a `<time>` element. Give it the date `2026-12-03` in its `datetime` attribute. Keep the period outside the element.

before: Read one idea and its worked markup.
Apply the idea to the small task.
Run the supported checks, then explain the changed case.

before.question: A time element stores datetime="2026-12-03". You change only its text to 4 December. Has its stored date changed?
choices: Yes, the browser rewrites datetime from the text.
No. The attribute still stores 3 December.
The element becomes a live calendar widget.
before.explanation: Attribute and content are separate. Update both deliberately so they do not conflict.

after.question: You change the words inside a time element, but leave datetime alone. Does the stored date change?
choices: Yes, it changes to match the words.
No. You must change datetime too.
after.explanation: The visible words and the datetime value are separate. Update both when the date changes.

before: Compare element meaning, attribute values and nesting with the visible example.
after: Keep the visible words exactly `Thursday, 3 December`.

project.task: Mark Thursday, 3 December with the stored date 2026-12-03.
